movement_source: row 'ROE – cash basis (%)', column 30 Jun 25 (Full Year Ended) -> column 30 Jun 26 (Full Year Ended)
headline: CBA's return on equity (cash basis) increased 50 basis points to 14.0% in FY26 from 13.5% in FY25. The bank states "The Bank's ROE increased 50bpts to 14.0% and remains peer leading" (ev-2); the results presentation corroborates "ROE (cash) 14.0% +50bpts" (ev-6) and "Cash ROE 13.5% 14.0% FY25 FY26" (ev-11). The statutory ROE also moved +0.5 ppt (13.4% to 13.9%), so the two bases show no material difference. The movement decomposes into a positive earnings effect (+0.96 ppt from 7.1% cash NPAT growth at constant equity) and a negative equity effect (−0.46 ppt from average equity growth of 3.3% at constant earnings), both derived, not disclosed.

drivers.bank_label: Movement in cash earnings at constant equity
drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed. Cash NPAT grew 7.1% (ev-6), from $10,253m to $10,982m (ev-1). At constant equity, prior-period ROE of 13.5% x 0.071 earnings growth lifts ROE by 0.96 ppt. The bank does not disclose this decomposition.

drivers.bank_label: Movement in average equity at constant earnings
drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed. Average equity grew from $75,710m to $78,238m (ev-1), up 3.3%; at constant earnings this lowers ROE by 0.46 ppt (total delta 0.5 minus earnings effect 0.96). Equity grew via retained earnings; the DRP is neutralised by on-market purchase (ev-12) and no share buy-back activity occurred in FY26 (ev-5).
The two derived contributions sum exactly to the total delta (0.96 − 0.46 = 0.50), so the interaction residual is zero. The bank does not disclose a separate interaction term.

notable_items: The bank deployed 72bpts of capital into credit risk weighted assets in FY26 with strong volume growth in commercial portfolios and domestic residential mortgages (ev-3).
The $1 billion on-market share buy-back, of which $300 million has been completed, expires on 12 August 2026 and will not be extended (ev-3); no buy-back activity was undertaken in FY26 (ev-5).

disagreements.explanation: The ratios table (ev-1) and the Group Performance Summary (ev-4) differ by $1m on FY25 cash NPAT, a rounding difference. The ROE table's own denominator uses 10,253.

limitations: The bank does not publish a ROE walk or bridge chart for this comparison; the earnings and equity effects are derived arithmetically from the ROE endpoints and the bank's stated 7.1% cash NPAT growth, not disclosed by the bank.
The equity effect is computed as a residual (total delta minus earnings effect) and therefore also absorbs the interaction term; the bank does not disclose a separate interaction decomposition.

The earnings growth rate used (7.1%) is the bank's stated cash NPAT growth (ev-6); the profit announcement's Group Performance Summary prints 7% (ev-4), a rounding difference that does not change the derived contributions materially.
